To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the double differential cross-sections for charged pion production by protons in the energy range of 3 GeV to 12 GeV on carbon, copper or tin targets are presented.

the pion cross-sections in pion production in pA collisions are larger than in pN collisions, and the cross-sections in the backward hemisphere are much larger than in the forward hemisphere, with the exception of the 3 GeV proton beam momentum where a large peak in the backward hemisphere is observed.

we have measured the double-differential production cross section of pions in the momentum range 100 MeVe/c<p<800 MeVe/c and in the angular range 0.35<θ<2.5 for pion production by protons on carbon (Cu and Sn) targets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the production of charged pion in proton–nucleus collisions.
the study of the production of charged pion in proton induced interactions.
the study of hadron–hadron interactions in the intermediate energy region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present data are in reasonable agreement with the existing data, but with the present precision, no significant deviation from the existing data is observed.
the data are in good agreement with the predictions from the HADRONS Monte Carlo generator, which is based on the FRITIOF 7.02 model.
the HARP results are in good agreement with other experiments and with model predictions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have measured the double-differential pion production cross-sections for the three target materials carbon, copper, and tin.
the results presented in this paper are the first measurements of charged pion production in proton–nucleus collisions in this energy range.
the results are consistent with previous data and that the present data are the first of their kind in this energy regime.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cross-sections for pion production are much larger than the predictions of the hadro-transport model UrQMD and that the cross-section data can be used as a benchmark to improve the models.
the pion double-differential cross section can be described by a single parameterization over the full phase space for a single beam energy.
, for all the incident momenta, there is a significant enhancement in the cross-section for pion production at forward angles, compared to the results of previous experiments.
